issues.legal_issue: A rape conviction cannot stand where the complainant was above the age at which consent is legally relevant and the evidence leaves a reasonable view that the intercourse was consensual.
material_facts: The trial court found the complainant was about 18 years old at the relevant time and acquitted the accused; the High Court reversed the acquittal and convicted him.
The complainant testified that she had sexual intercourse with the accused on several occasions, and the prosecution alleged that he had promised to marry her.
The complaint was lodged more than eight months after the alleged sexual relationship began and only a few days before the child’s birth.
The Supreme Court considered that a consensual-intercourse view was reasonably possible on the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The accused was entitled to the benefit of doubt; the appeal was allowed and the High Court’s judgment and order were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, sexual intercourse with a woman above 16 years of age is not rape if she consents. In a criminal case, where two views are reasonably possible on the evidence—one pointing to guilt and the other to innocence—the accused receives the benefit of doubt. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_after_acquittal_reversed and complainant_above_consent_relevant_age and complainant_described_repeated_intercourse and complaint_followed_long_delay and consensual_intercourse_view_reasonably_possible

predicates.criminal_appeal_after_acquittal_reversed: The case was a criminal appeal in which an appellate court had reversed a trial court acquittal and convicted the accused.
predicates.complainant_above_consent_relevant_age: The complainant was found to be above the age at which consent is legally relevant to whether intercourse constitutes rape.
predicates.complainant_described_repeated_intercour: The complainant testified that she had sexual intercourse with the accused on several occasions.
predicates.complaint_followed_long_delay: The complaint was made more than eight months after the alleged sexual relationship began and shortly before the child’s birth.
predicates.consensual_intercourse_view_reasonably_p: The evidence permitted a reasonable view that the complainant had consented to the intercourse.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows reversal of an acquittal, the complainant was above the consent-relevant age, the complainant described repeated intercourse, the complaint followed a long delay, and a consensual-intercourse view is reasonably possible, the accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt and the conviction is set aside.
